title: Parameterized small-bias Fourier estimation error
statement: Let $m$ be a positive integer, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $U$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinates, and let $\varepsilon,s\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<\varepsilon\le\tfrac12$ and $1\le s$. Suppose the sample's uniform pushforward density has every nonzero binary Fourier coefficient bounded in absolute value by $\varepsilon/s$, and the sum of the absolute values of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ is at most $s$. Then the absolute difference between the sample estimate of the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $U$ and its uniform Fourier coefficient is at most $\varepsilon$.
